title: Year-to-year weather did not explain the warm-and-dry community shift in 12 California grassland sites in 1983-2021; drought shifts reversed only partly
abstract: Question: California grassland plots changed toward species from warmer and drier places (Zhu, Song et al. 2024). Is this shift a reversible response to dry and hot years? Data: the public grassland-cfp v1.0.1 release (12 observational sites, 2,136 plot-years, 1983-2021) and NOAA nClimGrid growing-season (October-May) precipitation and temperature at each site. Method: plot-centred community temperature and precipitation indices (CTI, CPI; abundance and presence weights); site fixed-effects regressions with site-cluster bootstrap; reversal of the same plots after the 1987-1992 and 2012-2016 droughts; a forward test of 2012-2021 with models fitted up to 2011. Results: CTI increased 0.185 C per decade (95% interval 0.111 to 0.369); after weather adjustment it increased 0.173 C per decade (0.103 to 0.353). CPI decreased 32.7 mm per decade before and 31.5 mm per decade after adjustment. The year-to-year CTI slope was about 0.07 C per 1 C, but the CTI trend was about 0.7 of the local warming trend (0.26 C per decade). A pre-2012 weather model did not improve on persistence for 2012-2021; extension of pre-2012 site trends gave a smaller CTI error (difference 0.128 C, 0.051 to 0.202). After the 2012-2016 drought, 45% (25-66%) of the CTI rise reversed at McLaughlin annual grassland, in warm years; at Carrizo Plain CTI continued to rise. After the 1987-1992 drought, Jasper Ridge CTI reversed by about half but CPI continued to decrease. Previous-year rain raised exotic annual grass share and CPI. Limitations: 12 sites with unequal years, simple linear weather terms, short post-drought periods, source niche estimates, no sampling dates; nitrogen deposition, grazing and fire were not tested.
